text:
rachel: FYI bringing up vanguard-13b (hf -> redwood int3 experiment) on staging. small-prompt smoke shows stable logits but long-context repeats and odd token ID jumps after ~8k tokens.
Tony: hmm int3 huh. give quick numbers?
rachel: short: WikiQA EM fp16 72.1% -> int3 46.0%. perplexity jumps at 8k+. top1 token continuity breaks (repeats / shifted tokens).
igor: that pattern feels like a KV-cache indexing mismatch combined with rotary phase rounding at ultra-low precision. did the exporter include any `byte_order` or `kv_layout` flags?
meena: also check tokenizer: vanguard vocab has some 3-byte ligature sequences (not typical unicode NFKC) and some teams ship a custom utf8-normalizer. fast vs slow tokenizer differences can change byte offsets for cached chunks.
rachel: converter log: no `byte_order` field found; `kv_layout` defaulted to "contiguous_heads". I tried a quick re-convert with `--quant=int3 --proj_order=auto` and `--rotary_phase_shift=0.0` (default).
tony: try forcing `--byte_order=little` vs `--byte_order=big` — we've seen artifact exports where kernel packing flips endianness for packing low-bit ints. int3 packing is particularly sensitive.
igor: good call. also try a small rotary phase perturbation scan: some checkpoints used fractional phase offsets stored in a legacy tensor `rotary_phase_bias` (values ~0.125). if conversion ignores that, sin/cos tables are slightly off which accumulates over long contexts at int3.
meena: helper script to sweep both byte order and phase bias quickly:
```
for bo in ["little","big"]:
  for bias in [0.0, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25]:
    python tools/mini_onboard_probe.py \\
      --model vanguard.ckpt --quant=int3 --byte_order $bo --rotary_phase_bias $bias \\
      --suite wikiqa_long --max_ctx 16384 
```
meena: results on my laptop: (little,0.0) EM 46.0; (big,0.0) EM 45.8; (little,0.125) EM 70.9; (big,0.125) EM 71.2. bias=0.125 basically recovers fp16 numbers.
rachel: wild. so two things: (A) checkpoint contains rotary_phase_bias that our converter dropped; (B) int3 packing expects explicit byte_order metadata to choose correct pack/unpack. together they explain the longctx and token jump behavior.
ton y: are there tokenizer effects too?
meena: yes, small one: a 3-byte ligature (U+0F77 like) was normalized differently by HF fast tokenizer when `use_fast=True`. that shifts token boundaries for documents with those chars and shifts KV-cache offsets by one token for affected flows. in my sweep I used the slow tokenizer to avoid that.
igor: mitigation plan: (1) update convert pipeline to preserve `rotary_phase_bias*` tensors and apply them per-head when building sin/cos; (2) add explicit `byte_order` field to model metadata and use it during low-bit pack/unpack; (3) add `tokenizer_normalizer` step that folds the ligature to canonical form and emit `tokenizer_hash` in metadata; (4) add int3 pack/unpack regression tests with longctx suite.
rachel: created ticket RED-1002 with repro + logs. will open PR with small patches: propagate rotary_phase_bias into artifact and support `--byte_order` flag; also add a quick autodetect heuristic that tries bias candidates and picks the one with best longctx EM.
ton y: for autodetect, scan bias in [0, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4] and pick best avg EM across 10 short longctx prompts. if ambiguous, fall back to explicit user flag. add metadata keys: "rotary_phase_bias": "0.125", "byte_order": "little", "tokenizer_hash": "<hex>".
meena: also note in docs: int3 packing is not bitwise portable across different packer implementations unless byte_order is declared. Console should warn if a converted model's byte_order differs from runtime expectation.
igor: CI note: add an integration job that runs the 6-benchmark on overnight cluster for any model that sets quant<=int4.
onboarding-bot: issue RED-1002 created: "vanguard-13b int3 rotary_phase_bias + byte_order + tokenizer-ligature" assigned to rachel.
rachel: will open PR and attach mini_onboard_probe logs + failing prompt set. target quick fix OOD and full regression in nightly. will ping when PR is up.
meena: great. small follow-up: when we store rotary_phase_bias, ensure it's per-head or per-headgroup as checkpoint indicates mixed head granularity for vanguard. include in artifact metadata shape info.
ton y: thanks team. I'll reserve a GPU slot on staging cluster for full run tonight.
rachel: thanks all, dropping short logs and sample prompts in the RED-1002 ticket.
